jobs.description:
Senior Payments Operations Lead

Location: Remote
Employment: Full-time
Level: Senior individual contributor
Preferred geography: Ukraine or Eastern Europe

About the role

MCR Group builds and scales subscription-based digital products across international markets. Since launch, the company has grown 20x, and we are now building the payments infrastructure needed for our next stage of growth.

We are looking for a Senior Payments Operations Lead to own and develop our payment operations function. This is a hands-on individual-contributor role for someone who combines deep subscription-payments expertise with strong analytical, commercial, and operational skills.

You will have two core missions:

  1. Build our multi-PSP infrastructure: identify, negotiate with, onboard, and connect the right Payment Service Providers.
  2. Own ongoing payment performance: analyze transactions, identify problems and opportunities, and improve approval rates, renewal performance, and revenue recovery.

This is a greenfield opportunity. You will not inherit a mature payments organization or a fixed operating model. You will have the freedom and responsibility to build the function using your experience, judgment, and vision.

What you will own

Payment infrastructure and PSP strategy

  • Assess the current payment setup and define the future multi-PSP strategy.
  • Identify and evaluate new PSPs, acquirers, and payment partners.
  • Lead commercial negotiations, onboarding, contracting, and escalation processes.
  • Build a resilient multi-provider setup that reduces concentration and operational risk.
  • Design and implement payment orchestration, routing, cascading, and failover logic.
  • Work with legal, finance, product, and engineering teams throughout PSP integrations.
  • Establish a structured approach to PSP performance reviews and relationship management.

The initial infrastructure-building phase is expected to be especially intensive during the first six months. Once the core setup is established, the focus will shift toward continuous optimization and maintenance.

Payment performance and daily operations

  • Monitor payment performance across all PSPs, products, countries, and transaction types.
  • Analyze authorization rates, decline rates, decline reasons, renewal sequences, and payment failures.
  • Identify performance issues and revenue opportunities through daily analysis.
  • Define retry, cascading, routing, and dunning strategies.
  • Improve failed-payment recovery and reduce involuntary churn.
  • Build or request the reports needed to make informed operational decisions.
  • Create dashboards, alerts, and monitoring processes that identify payment issues before they materially affect revenue.
  • Investigate changes in performance and coordinate corrective actions with internal teams and external providers.

As additional PSPs are connected, the analytical and operational complexity of the role will grow. Strong attention to detail and comfort working with numbers every day are essential.

Risk, disputes, and process ownership

  • Build and manage the operational framework for disputes, refunds, chargebacks, and fraud monitoring.
  • Analyze related reports, trends, ratios, and root causes.
  • Define responsibilities, workflows, escalation paths, and internal controls.
  • Maintain compliance with PSP risk programs and relevant card-scheme requirements.
  • Partner with the team member responsible for processing individual refunds and chargebacks.

You will not be expected to handle every individual refund or dispute personally. Your responsibility will be to understand these processes deeply, build the right structure, monitor results, and ensure the function operates effectively.

What we are looking for

Essential experience

  • At least five years of relevant experience in payment operations, payment performance, acquiring, or subscription billing.
  • Direct experience working with multiple PSPs, such as Stripe, Adyen, Braintree, Checkout.com, or comparable providers.
  • Proven experience evaluating and onboarding PSPs and managing multi-provider payment setups.
  • Experience building or operating payment orchestration, routing, and cascading systems.
  • Strong experience with recurring subscriptions, renewals, retries, dunning, and involuntary-churn reduction.
  • Experience managing more than $12 million in payment volume.
  • Strong knowledge of payment metrics, including authorization rates, decline reasons, recovery rates, dispute ratios, and fraud ratios.
  • Deep understanding of refunds, disputes, chargebacks, fraud monitoring, and card-scheme requirements.
  • Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate payment data into clear priorities and actions.
  • Experience building reporting, dashboards, and operational monitoring from the ground up.
  • Confidence working directly with senior executives, technical teams, legal partners, and external payment providers.
  • Strong English communication and negotiation skills.

Particularly relevant backgrounds

We are especially interested in candidates from high-volume, international subscription businesses, consumer applications, digital products, SaaS, streaming, or comparable recurring-revenue environments.

Experience limited to one-time payments or sectors with fundamentally different PSP-rotation models may be less relevant unless accompanied by substantial subscription-payment expertise.

What success looks like

During your first six months, you will be expected to:

  • Build a clear understanding of our payment flows, performance, risks, and reporting gaps.
  • Define the target PSP and payment-orchestration strategy.
  • Establish reliable payment-performance reporting and operational alerts.
  • Lead the evaluation, negotiation, and onboarding of additional PSPs.
  • Create structured processes for payment incidents, disputes, fraud, and PSP escalations.
  • Identify and begin implementing opportunities to improve authorization and renewal performance.

Over time, success will be measured through:

  • Stronger approval and renewal rates.
  • Higher failed-payment recovery.
  • Lower involuntary churn.
  • Greater PSP resilience and lower concentration risk.
  • Healthy fraud and dispute ratios.
  • Reliable reporting and faster incident detection.
  • Sustainable payment infrastructure that supports new products and markets.

Specific targets will be agreed based on current performance baselines.

Reporting and collaboration

You will have one administrative manager responsible for performance reviews, goal-setting, and day-to-day organizational support.

Functionally, you will work closely with:

  • The CEO on payment strategy and business priorities.
  • The CFO on financial performance, risk, and commercial matters.
  • The founders on major payment-infrastructure decisions.
  • Product and engineering on integrations and payment-flow improvements.
  • Legal and operational colleagues on contracts, compliance, disputes, refunds, and fraud processes.

Because this is a new position, the final organizational structure may evolve as the function develops.

Why join us

  • Build a critical payment function from the ground up.
  • Define the infrastructure based on your own knowledge and vision.
  • Work on an international subscription business that has grown 20x.
  • Support new products and expansion into new markets.
  • Own decisions with direct impact on revenue, retention, and business resilience.
  • Work directly with the founders on a strategic company priority.
  • Receive highly competitive compensation based on your experience, impact, and fit.
  • Work remotely with a fast-moving, predominantly Ukrainian team.
Salary: $3,000 – $4,500 / month

Position Summary

The Chief Compliance Officer (CCO) – Wealth Management is responsible for designing, implementing, and overseeing the compliance and regulatory framework for the wealth management business. The CCO ensures adherence to applicable securities laws, fiduciary obligations, anti-money laundering regulations, privacy requirements, and industry standards while promoting a culture of integrity, ethical conduct, and regulatory excellence.

The role serves as the primary advisor to executive leadership and the Board on compliance matters and provides independent oversight of regulatory risks across wealth advisory, private banking, investment management, brokerage, trust, and fiduciary services.

Key Responsibilities

Compliance Strategy & Governance

  • Develop and execute the enterprise-wide compliance strategy for the wealth management division.
  • Establish and maintain compliance policies, procedures, and governance frameworks.
  • Ensure compliance programs align with business objectives and regulatory expectations.
  • Advise executive leadership and the Board on emerging regulatory developments and compliance risks.
  • Promote a strong culture of ethics, integrity, and regulatory accountability.

Regulatory Compliance Oversight

  • Ensure compliance with applicable securities, investment advisory, fiduciary, and banking regulations.
  • Monitor regulatory developments and assess their impact on the organization.
  • Oversee regulatory examinations, inspections, and inquiries.
  • Coordinate responses to regulators and ensure timely remediation of findings.
  • Maintain effective relationships with regulatory authorities and industry bodies.

Wealth Management & Advisory Compliance

  • Oversee compliance programs covering:
    • Investment Advisory Services
    • Private Banking
    • Brokerage Services
    • Trust and Fiduciary Services
    • Retirement and Estate Planning Services
    • Discretionary Portfolio Management
  • Review new products, investment strategies, and business initiatives for regulatory compliance.
  • Ensure adherence to suitability, fiduciary, and best-interest obligations.

Financial Crime Compliance

  • Oversee Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) programs.
  • Ensure compliance with sanctions screening and anti-bribery regulations.
  • Monitor suspicious activity reporting and transaction surveillance programs.
  • Assess financial crime risks associated with clients, products, and jurisdictions.
  • Coordinate investigations and regulatory reporting requirements.

Surveillance, Monitoring & Testing

  • Establish risk-based compliance monitoring and testing programs.
  • Oversee employee trade surveillance and conflict-of-interest management.
  • Conduct periodic compliance reviews and control assessments.
  • Monitor client communications, marketing materials, and investment recommendations.
  • Ensure corrective actions are implemented for identified compliance issues.

Fiduciary & Conduct Risk Management

  • Ensure compliance with fiduciary duties and client best-interest standards.
  • Oversee management of conflicts of interest and disclosure requirements.
  • Promote fair treatment of clients and ethical business practices.
  • Assess conduct risks associated with advisor and relationship manager activities.

Training & Awareness

  • Develop compliance training programs for advisors, bankers, and employees.
  • Promote awareness of regulatory obligations and ethical standards.
  • Ensure timely completion of mandatory compliance certifications.
  • Provide advisory support to business units on compliance matters.

Reporting & Board Engagement

  • Prepare compliance reports for executive leadership, risk committees, and the Board.
  • Present compliance risk assessments, monitoring results, and regulatory updates.
  • Develop key compliance indicators (KCIs) and compliance dashboards.
  • Escalate significant compliance issues and regulatory concerns.

Leadership & Team Development

  • Lead and develop compliance professionals across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Build a high-performance compliance function.
  • Foster collaboration with legal, risk, audit, operations, and business teams.
  • Support succession planning and talent development initiatives.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Law, Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.
  • Master's degree, MBA, Juris Doctor (JD), or equivalent advanced qualification preferred.

Professional Certifications

Preferred certifications include:

  • Certified Regulatory Compliance Manager (CRCM)
  • Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS)
  • Investment Adviser Certified Compliance Professional (IACCP)
  • Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA)
  • Bar admission or legal qualifications may be advantageous.

Experience

  • 12–15+ years of compliance, legal, regulatory, or risk management experience.
  • Significant experience within wealth management, private banking, asset management, or brokerage environments.
  • Experience interacting with regulators, boards, and executive leadership teams.
  • Demonstrated success leading enterprise compliance programs.
  • Strong knowledge of fiduciary and investment advisory regulations.

Technical Competencies

  • Wealth Management Compliance

  • Investment Advisory Compliance

  • Financial Crime Prevention

  • Risk-Based Decision Making

jobs.excerpt: About LucidyaLucidya is an AI-native platform for customer experience (CX) intelligence that helps organizations understand, engage, and retain customers at scale.
jobs.description:
About Lucidya

Lucidya is an AI-native platform for customer experience (CX) intelligence that helps organizations understand, engage, and retain customers at scale.

Unlike traditional platforms that stop at reporting and dashboards, Lucidya combines proprietary AI, deep language understanding, and autonomous workflows to help organizations move from insight to action. Our technology is built in-house and trained on millions of multilingual customer conversations, enabling brands across the MENA region to make better decisions, deliver better experiences, and build stronger customer relationships.

As AI reshapes how businesses operate, we're building products that make customer understanding faster, more accurate, and more actionable than ever before.

Why This Role Matters

Most organizations today are overwhelmed with customer data.

Conversations are happening across social media, surveys, reviews, support tickets, messaging channels, and countless other touchpoints. The challenge isn't collecting the data anymore. It's knowing what matters and what to do next.

The Monitoring & Research domain sits at the center of that challenge.

This is where customers come to understand public perception, identify emerging trends, monitor competitors, measure customer sentiment, and uncover the insights that drive business decisions. It is one of the most strategically important parts of Lucidya's platform and one of the biggest opportunities for innovation as AI transforms how research and customer intelligence are done.

As Senior Product Manager, you'll be responsible for shaping how thousands of users discover, trust, and act on insights generated from millions of customer conversations.

You'll be joining a team that values ownership over hierarchy, customer outcomes over feature output, and learning over certainty. We move quickly, challenge assumptions, and expect product leaders to bring strong opinions while remaining open to changing their minds when the evidence says otherwise.

If you're excited by complex customer problems, AI-powered products, and the opportunity to define the future of customer intelligence in a region where world-class solutions are still emerging, this role will give you significant room to make an impact.

What You'll Do

Own the future of Monitoring & Research at Lucidya

You'll define the vision, strategy, and roadmap across three key product areas:

  • Social Listening
  • Managed Channels Analytics
  • Voice of Customer (VoC)

Your responsibility isn't simply delivering features. It's ensuring customers can confidently answer critical business questions about their customers, markets, competitors, and brand performance.

Turn customer signals into decisions

You'll spend significant time understanding how customers currently make decisions, where they struggle to find trustworthy insights, and what prevents them from taking action.

You'll use those learnings to build products that help customers move beyond reporting and toward clear recommendations, meaningful insights, and measurable business outcomes.

Lead discovery before delivery

You'll challenge assumptions, validate problems, and ensure we're solving issues that matter before resources are committed.

You'll regularly engage customers, prospects, Customer Success teams, and internal stakeholders to uncover opportunities and validate product direction.

Success in this role means building the right thing, not simply building things quickly.

Raise the quality bar for AI-powered insights

As AI becomes increasingly central to our platform, you'll help define what "trustworthy AI" means in practice.

You'll work closely with AI, Data, Design, and Engineering teams to improve:

  • Insight accuracy
  • Sentiment quality
  • Explainability
  • Relevance
  • Customer trust

You'll constantly ask whether an insight is genuinely useful, not just technically impressive.

Make difficult prioritization decisions

Not every good idea belongs on the roadmap.

You'll evaluate opportunities using customer feedback, product data, market insights, commercial priorities, and strategic impact.

You'll make trade-offs transparently and help the organization understand why certain bets are worth making while others are not.

Drive product adoption and business impact

You'll closely monitor customer behavior, adoption patterns, retention drivers, churn signals, and feedback loops.

You'll use those insights to continuously improve the product and ensure the work being delivered creates measurable value for both customers and the business.

Be a leader beyond product

You'll collaborate across Engineering, Design, AI, Customer Success, Sales, Marketing, and Leadership teams.

You'll help create alignment, provide clarity during ambiguity, and contribute to building a culture where teams are empowered to solve problems rather than simply execute requirements.

Requirements

Who You Are

You have strong product fundamentals

You have at least 5 years of product management experience, ideally within B2B SaaS environments.

You know how to take a problem from discovery through validation, delivery, measurement, and iteration.

You understand that product management is ultimately about creating customer and business value, not managing backlogs.

You simplify complexity

You're comfortable working with large datasets, analytics platforms, AI-powered products, or technically complex systems.

More importantly, you know how to transform complexity into experiences that feel intuitive and useful to customers.

You stay close to customers

You don't rely solely on internal opinions to make decisions.

You regularly speak with customers, investigate workflows, validate assumptions, and seek evidence before committing to a direction.

You're naturally curious about how people work and where products create friction in their lives.

You are comfortable making decisions with incomplete information

You won't always have perfect data.

You can balance analysis with action, make informed decisions under uncertainty, and adapt when new information becomes available.

You communicate with clarity

You can explain technical concepts to non-technical audiences and customer problems to technical teams.

You build alignment through clear thinking, structured communication, and transparency.

You care about outcomes

You measure success by customer adoption, customer value, and business impact rather than the number of features released.

You're willing to challenge existing thinking when you believe there's a better way to solve a problem.

Bonus Points If You Have

  • Experience with social listening, media monitoring, Voice of Customer, customer intelligence, or research platforms
  • Experience building AI-powered, analytics-heavy, or data-intensive products
  • Familiarity with sentiment analysis, NLP, LLMs, recommendation systems, or automated research workflows
  • Experience working with Arabic-language products, dialects, or regional customer behaviors
  • Knowledge of MENA markets, particularly Saudi Arabia and the GCC
  • Experience with platforms such as Brandwatch, Sprinklr, Meltwater, Talkwalker, Qualtrics, Medallia, or Brand24

What Success Looks Like

Within your first 12 months:

  • Customers trust Lucidya's insights enough to use them in critical business decisions
  • Product adoption and engagement across Monitoring & Research increase meaningfully
  • AI-powered insight experiences become more accurate, actionable, and differentiated
  • Clear product strategy and prioritization frameworks are established across the domain
  • Customer feedback consistently influences roadmap decisions
  • Cross-functional teams have strong alignment around goals, priorities, and outcomes

Lucidya is an equal opportunity employer. We believe great teams are built through diverse experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds. If you're excited about the opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply anyway.

jobs.excerpt: Full-Time · Remote (Canada) · Eterio Realities Inc.
jobs.description:
Full-Time · Remote (Canada) · Eterio Realities Inc. / Fabstation

[Salary range: $ 160,000 - 200,000 CAD

About the Role

Fabstation puts AR work instructions directly onto structural steel during fabrication. Our software runs on AR tablets and headsets on real shop floors across North America, overlaying CAD-driven guidance onto multi-tonne steel assemblies during fit-up, welding, and inspection. We are cash-flow positive, growing fast, and used daily in production.

We are hiring a Senior Computer Vision Engineer to own our real-time 3D object tracking capability: locking a CAD model onto a physical steel member and keeping it locked as the user moves around it. Tracking is core to our product, and we build it in-house.

You will build on internal groundwork already underway and own the road from there: architecture, implementation, optimization, and production hardening. This is a role for someone who wants to own a hard, central problem end-to-end and see it shipped into the hands of real tradespeople, not maintain someone else's pipeline.

What You'll Do

  • Own the on-device object tracking core end-to-end, from architecture through production
  • Design and implement real-time, model-based 6DoF pose estimation and continuous tracking for textureless steel structures, using CAD models as the tracking reference
  • Fuse object tracking with platform world tracking (visual-inertial odometry), depth, and IMU data; own tracking-loss detection, drift management, and recovery
  • Optimize native C++ vision pipelines for iOS and Apple silicon: rendering, CPU/GPU budgets, and sustained frame rates on iPad or headset hardware
  • Extend tracking to large structures: partial visibility, multi-region strategies, and CAD mesh preprocessing from IFC/STEP - type exports
  • Integrate native modules with Unity via a plugin bridge, and work with our Unity team from prototype through release
  • Define tracking quality metrics and benchmark against real shop-floor conditions: occlusion, mixed lighting, and cluttered scenes of visually similar material

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of professional experience in computer vision or a closely related field, with a focus on real-time systems
  • Shipped at least one real-time computer vision feature on a mobile platform (iOS or Android)
  • Strong modern C++; Python is an asset
  • Solid foundation in 3D geometry: camera models, calibration, projective geometry, and linear algebra
  • Working command of nonlinear least-squares optimization (Gauss–Newton / Levenberg–Marquardt) and pose parameterization on SE(3)
  • Hands-on experience with pose estimation and object tracking algorithms
  • Experience integrating native C++ libraries with Unity, or equivalent native-mobile plugin experience
  • Strong profiling and optimization skills on ARM (frame budgets, Instruments or equivalent)
  • Working proficiency with OpenCV

Preferred Qualifications

  • Model-based 3D object tracking (region-based, edge-based, or hybrid approaches)
  • Metal and GPU compute on Apple silicon
  • Visual-inertial odometry or SLAM; ARKit (ARCore an asset)
  • State estimation and multi-sensor fusion: Kalman filtering, factor graphs (Ceres, g2o, GTSAM), extrinsic calibration, and time synchronization
  • On-device ML deployment: Core ML, ONNX Runtime, or Unity Sentis; learning-based pose estimation or refinement that has shipped on-device
  • CAD data handling: mesh processing and decimation, IFC/STEP-style exports
  • Background in industrial vision, robotics, or augmented reality

How to Apply

We prioritize applications that demonstrate hands-on, real-time computer vision work. Please include:

  • A brief introduction and a summary of relevant experience
  • Links to your GitHub profile, portfolio, or publications
  • One or two examples of real-time pose estimation, tracking, or 3D vision work you built, links or short write-ups

Working at Eterio

Eterio Realities Inc. (Victoria, BC) is the company behind Fabstation, an AR-enabled manufacturing execution system for structural steel fabrication. We are a small senior team; you will have direct ownership, direct access to real customer shop floors, and a short path from your code to a tradesperson's hands.

Eterio Realities is an equal opportunity employer. Applicants must be legally authorized to work in Canada.

Salary: $160,000 – $200,000 / year

jobs.description:
Fire Sprinkler Design Engineer – Independent Contractor (Ukraine)

Location: Ukraine, Remote
Industry: Mission-Critical Facilities, Data Centers
Engagement Type: Independent Contractor Agreement for Provision of Services (Long-Term)

Ehvert Mission Critical, a business unit within Salas O’Brien, is seeking an experienced Fire Sprinkler Design Engineer for a long-term independent contractor engagement.

This is an ongoing contractual engagement with a US-based company and is not limited to a single project. The role involves continuous collaboration across multiple mission-critical projects, based on business needs.

You will provide services as an independent, self-employed professional under a formal independent contractor agreement.

How to Apply: Interested candidates should submit their resume in English detailing their relevant experience.

Role Summary

We are seeking a skilled Fire Sprinkler Design Engineerto support the design and coordination of fire sprinkler and suppression systems for cutting-edge data center projects across the U.S.

In this role, you will be responsible for designing, modeling, and coordinating fire sprinkler systems, including wet, dry, pre-action, and deluge systems. You will prepare hydraulic calculations, sprinkler layouts, engineering documentation, and detailed designs while ensuring compliance with applicable fire protection codes and standards.

You will work closely with multidisciplinary engineering teams in a collaborative, fast-paced environment and contribute throughout the project lifecycle, from schematic design through detailed design and execution.

Strong technical expertise in sprinkler system design, attention to detail, and excellent communication skills are essential.

What We Offer

  • Experience in a high-tech industry completing work for an international company
  • Unique, cutting-edge data center projects
  • Dynamic work partnering with a team of professionals focused on engineering
  • Competitive hourly rate
  • Ability to collaborate remotely
  • Supportive dynamic environment
  • English classes made available

Key Responsibilities

  • Using BIM tools to model and coordinate fire sprinkler systems with other disciplines; hands-on Autodesk Revit experience is a must
  • Designing fire sprinkler and suppression systems, including wet, dry, pre-action, and deluge systems
  • Developing sprinkler layouts and detailed fire protection designs for mission-critical facilities
  • Preparing hydraulic calculations and other engineering calculations required for sprinkler system design
  • Selecting and laying out sprinkler heads, piping, valves, and associated fire protection equipment
  • Developing a thorough understanding and delivery of project requirements as they relate to scope, cost, and schedule
  • Determining and expediting engineering deliverables for projects
  • Developing and maintaining project scope of work documentation and revisions as required during design evolution
  • Ensuring compliance with applicable fire protection codes and standards, including NFPA, IBC, and IFC
  • Preparing technical documentation required for project execution, including design criteria, calculations, specifications, and equipment data sheets
  • Reviewing shop drawings and submittals for compliance with design intent
  • Producing coordinated models and drawings using BIM and CAD tools
  • Coordinating sprinkler systems with architectural, structural, mechanical, and electrical disciplines
  • Performing occasional site visits to support construction progress (valid U.S. work visa considered an asset but not required)

Qualifications & Experience

  • A bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering (fire protection, mechanical, or related field)
  • At least 4–5 years of experience in fire sprinkler/fire protection design
  • Proven expertise in the design of fire sprinkler and suppression systems
  • Strong understanding of wet, dry, pre-action, and deluge sprinkler systems
  • Experience performing and reviewing hydraulic calculations
  • Knowledge of applicable fire protection codes and standards, including NFPA, IBC, and IFC; FM Global knowledge is a plus
  • Hands-on experience with Autodesk Revit – is a must
  • Experience designing systems for industrial, commercial, or mission-critical projects
  • Written and spoken English B1 and higher
  • Microsoft Office proficiency (Word, Excel, Outlook)
  • Ability to multi-task and prioritize while meeting project deadlines
  • Self-starter, ambitious, and able to thrive in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong communication skills and ability to explain technical concepts clearly
  • Experience with U.S.-based projects and data centers is considered an advantage

Why Us?

  • Perform on high-profile, hyperscale, and AI data center projects in a rapidly expanding industry
  • Collaborate with leading professionals and global clients such as Microsoft, Oracle, Uber, and Amazon
  • Competitive terms of the contract
  • Dynamic environment fostering creativity through exposure to advanced technologies such as BIM, VDC, digital twins, and augmented reality

Collaborate with Ehvert Mission Critical, a business unit within Salas O’Brien, and help us achieve our international engineering goals!

Ehvert Mission Critical specializes in the design and construction management of data centers. We are a business unit within Salas O’Brien — a 4,000-person engineering and professional services firm, widely recognized for its extensive expertise and impressive project portfolio. With more than 10,000 projects annually and 100 offices across North America, Salas O'Brien is ranked #39 on Engineering News-Record’s 2024 Top 500 Design Firms list.

Ehvert Mission Critical, a business unit within Salas O’Brien, is an industry leader in data center facility engineering, specializing in hyperscale and AI data centers, designing massive data centers for global tech giants like Microsoft, Uber, Oracle, and Amazon. Our projects involve complex electrical, mechanical, fire protection, automation, and security systems necessary to power, cool, and secure these high-demand facilities, often exceeding loads of 100 MW per facility and up to 500 MW per site.

We are recognized for our advanced engineering and construction techniques, including Building Information Modeling (BIM), Virtual Design and Construction (VDC), and augmented reality.

We offer highly competitive service fees to our independent contractors.

This engagement is strictly as an independent contractor. You will not be eligible for any employee benefits, and we will not withhold taxes, provide insurance(s), or make contributions to social security/pensions on your behalf. You are responsible for complying with all tax and labor obligations in your country of residence. A formal independent contractor agreement will be required before work begins, governed by Texas, United States law.

For more information, visit Ehvert and Salas O’Brien websites.

jobs.excerpt: Job OverviewWe are seeking a highly experienced Senior Linux Infrastructure Engineer with deep expertise in Linux administration, bare metal infrastructure, enterprise storage, and next-generation AI Factory / GPU infrastructure platforms.

Job Overview

We are seeking a highly experienced Senior Linux Infrastructure Engineer with deep expertise in Linux administration, bare metal infrastructure, enterprise storage, and next-generation AI Factory / GPU infrastructure platforms. This role is focused on designing, deploying, operating, and troubleshooting large-scale Linux-based infrastructure that powers both traditional enterprise workloads and modern AI/ML environments.

This is not a DevOps-focused role. We already have a dedicated DevOps team and are looking for an engineer with extensive hands-on experience in Bare Metal as a Service (BMaaS), GPU infrastructure, high-performance storage, data center operations, and enterprise Linux platforms.

The ideal candidate will have experience building and managing infrastructure from the hardware layer up, including servers, networking, storage, GPU clusters, and AI-ready platforms. They should be comfortable working with high-performance computing (HPC), AI Factory environments, and large-scale Linux deployments where performance, reliability, and operational excellence are critical.

Key Responsibilities & Required Skills

Linux & Bare Metal Infrastructure

  • Expert-level Linux administration (Ubuntu required; Red Hat and SUSE preferred)
  • Deep expertise in bare metal server deployment, architecture, provisioning, and lifecycle management
  • Experience operating Bare Metal as a Service (BMaaS) platforms and large-scale infrastructure environments
  • Strong understanding of server hardware, including:
    • BIOS/UEFI
    • RAID controllers
    • Firmware management
    • iLO/iDRAC/IPMI
    • NICs and SmartNICs
    • HBA cards
    • Hardware diagnostics and troubleshooting

AI Factory & GPU Infrastructure

  • Knowledge of AI Factory architecture and infrastructure requirements

    • GPU resource allocation and scheduling
    • Multi-GPU systems
    • GPU networking requirements
    • High-bandwidth, low-latency infrastructure design
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA ecosystem technologies such as:
    • CUDA
    • NCCL
    • GPUDirect Storage
    • NVIDIA Fabric Manager
    • NVIDIA Base Command (preferred)

Enterprise Storage & Data Platforms

  • Advanced Linux storage administration:
    • LVM
    • XFS, EXT4
    • NFS
    • iSCSI
    • Fibre Channel SAN
    • Multipath I/O
  • Strong hands-on experience with Ceph, including:
    • Cluster architecture
    • MON, OSD, MDS
    • RBD, CephFS, RGW
    • Capacity planning
    • Performance tuning
    • Failure recovery
  • Experience with high-performance AI storage platforms such as:
    • WEKA
    • VAST Data
    • Dell PowerScale
    • Pure Storage FlashBlade
    • NetApp
  • Understanding of:
    • NVMe-over-Fabrics (NVMe-oF)
    • RDMA
    • GPUDirect Storage
    • Parallel file systems
    • AI data pipelines

Networking & Infrastructure

  • Strong networking knowledge:
    • Bonding
    • VLANs
    • Routing
    • MTU optimization
    • DNS
    • DHCP
  • Experience with high-performance data center networking:
    • 100G/200G/400G Ethernet
    • RoCE
    • RDMA
    • Spine-Leaf architectures
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA Spectrum-X, Mellanox/NVIDIA ConnectX adapters, or equivalent technologies
  • Strong understanding of Layer 2 and Layer 3 infrastructure design and troubleshooting

Operations & Reliability

  • Experience with high availability, clustering, and disaster recovery
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across:
    • Linux operating systems
    • Hardware platforms
    • GPU infrastructure
    • Networking
    • Enterprise storage
  • Experience supporting mission-critical production environments
  • Bash and Python scripting for automation and operational efficiency
  • Experience creating operational documentation, runbooks, and infrastructure standards

Nice to Have

  • Kubernetes infrastructure (especially AI/ML and GPU integration)
  • KVM, VMware, OpenShift Virtualization, or similar virtualization platforms
  • Ansible automation
  • NVIDIA Base Command Manager
  • Slurm or HPC workload schedulers
  • Observability and monitoring platforms (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry)
  • Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) tools
  • IPAM solutions
  • AWS, Azure, or hybrid cloud exposure

We Are Not Looking For

  • Candidates whose experience is primarily CI/CD pipeline engineering
  • Engineers focused mainly on Terraform, GitOps, or application delivery pipelines
  • Cloud-only administrators with limited bare metal, storage, or hardware experience
  • Professionals whose primary expertise is software development rather than infrastructure engineering

Ideal Candidate

Someone who has spent years designing, building, and operating enterprise Linux environments, large-scale bare metal infrastructure, storage platforms, and modern AI Factory environments. The ideal candidate understands how to deploy and manage GPU-enabled infrastructure, BMaaS platforms, enterprise storage, and high-performance networking while solving complex operating system, hardware, storage, and AI infrastructure challenges. DevOps experience is a plus, but deep Linux, infrastructure, storage, BMaaS, and AI Factory expertise is the primary requirement.

jobs.excerpt: Maybe you call yourself an Internal Communications Manager, a Content Strategist, a Wordsmith-for-Hire, a Chief "Let-Me-Just-Rewrite-That"… or maybe you just call yourself Alex.
jobs.description:
Maybe you call yourself an Internal Communications Manager, a Content Strategist, a Wordsmith-for-Hire, a Chief "Let-Me-Just-Rewrite-That"… or maybe you just call yourself Alex. Whatever title you use, you're the person who takes a messy, half-formed brief and turns it into something people actually want to read, watch, or click through.

What you get

  • €68,000–€78,000 gross per year, based on your experience.
  • €5,000 a year for your own growth, with a real say in how you spend it.
  • 25 vacation days + the option to buy up to 10 more + local public holidays + the option of a sabbatical up to 4 months.
  • Two trips abroad a year with the whole team + occasional drinks and team outings.
  • €500 home-office budget and a great laptop.
  • A well-earned “Hey, well done Buddy!”, now and then.
  • Fully remote, from anywhere in the Netherlands.

Benefits across Europe: the perks above are AYBI’s and go to everyone, everywhere. Statutory benefits (pension, health, social security, leave, sick pay, notice) follow the hire’s country via their local contract or EOR.

About us

All Your BI is a remote-first data agency based in Rotterdam. Since 2019 we’ve grown from a boutique consultancy into an international data team of more than 60 data heroes spread across Europe. We deliver managed BI services for logistics and industrial companies, helping reduce data waste and move businesses forward. We live for the WOW moment, that sparkle in users’ eyes when they gain new insights and discover opportunities. We work according to Holacracy: little hierarchy, lots of ownership. Serious work. Serious fun.

What the job looks like

  • Own our internal communication voice. Company-wide updates, Town Halls and everything in between should sound like All Your BI, not corporate filler.
  • Take a messy, half-formed brief and turn it into a message people actually read: the right words, the right structure, the right length.
  • Build our change muscle by thinking beyond the announcement. What do people need to understand? Where are they likely to get stuck? What actually helps a change land?
  • Own the communication side of change initiatives end to end, building whatever mix of messages, presentations, videos, guides and FAQs the moment calls for.
  • Design and help deliver our Town Halls. Pull together input from across the company, shape the story, build the presentation, prep the presenters, and run the session.
  • Create and coordinate our company-wide communications, keeping our remote, distributed team informed and connected.
  • Keep our People Handbook and other Confluence spaces genuinely easy to use, and help other teams do the same in their own spaces.
  • Take someone else's complex or messy information and turn it into a presentation that's actually clear and easy to follow.
  • Pick the right format for the moment. Sometimes that's a two-minute video, sometimes five slides, sometimes a live session, and sometimes it's deciding we don't need another communication at all.
  • Track how communication is landing and use what you learn to make the next one better.
  • Occasionally help design a learning experience alongside our P&C Lead, and turn a subject-matter expert's know-how into something others can use.
  • Provide some L&D support: keeping tabs on certifications and helping maintain our Udemy setup.

Requirements

What you bring

  • A genuine wordsmith: fluency in English at the level where you catch tone, subtext and register instinctively, not just vocabulary and grammar. You can tighten, restructure, and simplify without losing what the sentence was actually trying to say.
  • Content creation, not just copy: confident building the visual side too — presentations, video edits, and similar — using whatever tools get you there fast, AI included.
  • A good eye: you can spot when something is confusing, too long, visually messy, or unnecessarily corporate, and you know how to fix it.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: you can take a rough brief, ask the right questions, and build something real without needing everything spelled out first.
  • Ownership: you manage your own pieces of work end to end and get things over the line without much hand-holding.
  • Collaborative: you’ll own a lot, but very little of it will be created in isolation.

We’re a growing team across Europe, and we hire to widen that mix, not narrow it. What matters is what you can do and the perspective you bring, not your age, gender, ethnicity, orientation, disability, background, or where you studied. If the role excites you and you bring most of it, apply: the people who add the most rarely tick every box.

Highlights

You'll turn messy briefs into internal comms and content people actually read: Town Halls, change stories, videos and decks for a remote-first team across Europe.

jobs.description:
ABOUT VICTORY LIVE
Victory Live is a private equity backed technology company aimed at maximizing distribution and yield for live event ticket inventory. We provide an end-to-end software platform for the live ticketing industry, managing thousands of sports, theater, and live music event tickets on behalf of artists, promoters, teams, venues, and professional resellers. Victory Live’s comprehensive offerings include an established B2B marketplace, along with both a full-service and an automated SaaS platform to handle all elements of the ticket sales lifecycle, from ingestion to sales fulfillment.

THE POSITION
Victory Live is looking for an Engineering Manager to lead a team of engineers working across our Ruby, Python, and .NET services. This isn't a pure people-manager role. You'll bring real technical depth, help set architectural direction, and be the person your team looks to when there's no clear answer. You'll also think ahead: understand where your domain needs to go, make the bets, and connect that strategy to your team's day-to-day work.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead and mentor your team, holding a bar for technical excellence, delivery, and stakeholder satisfaction across the engineers who report to you.
  • Set technical direction. Guide architecture and technology decisions for your team's systems, working across Ruby, Python, and .NET as the work requires.
  • Stay hands-on. Spend roughly 5–10% of your time in code reviews, architectural guidance, and hands-on debugging during critical incidents.
  • Translate strategy into execution. Define where your domain needs to be in 12–24 months, turn that into team bets and priorities, and own that narrative with stakeholders.
  • Partner cross-functionally. Align technical strategy with product, business, and other engineering teams, and turn high-level vision into actionable plans.
  • Build the team. Hire, develop, and retain engineers, and create a culture where people do their best work and grow.
  • Drive AI-native practices. Model and push adoption of Claude Code, Copilot, and agentic workflows as a standard part of how your team ships.
  • Own delivery. Plan capacity, manage tradeoffs, and negotiate scope with stakeholders without compromising quality or team health.

REQUIREMENTS

  • 8+ years of software engineering experience across production systems.
  • 3+ years of engineering management experience, with a track record of shipping business-impactful work.
  • Demonstrated ability to set technical strategy and connect it to team execution, not just manage delivery.
  • Strong technical depth in at least one of our core stacks (Ruby on Rails, Python/FastAPI, or C#/.NET), with the ability to speak credibly across the others.
  • Proven ability to attract, retain, and develop engineering talent.
  • Active, deliberate use of AI-powered development tools, with a track record of driving adoption on a team.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, with the ability to build trust across engineering and non-engineering stakeholders.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience managing distributed teams across onshore and offshore locations.
  • Background in ticketing, marketplaces, e-commerce, or other high-transaction consumer platforms.
  • Experience leading a team through an acquisition, platform consolidation, or major system migration.

WHY VICTORY LIVE

  • You'll build the infrastructure live events run on; millions of tickets, hundreds of venues, many of the largest teams and events in the world.
  • A lean team where decisions move fast and your code reaches real fans, often the same week.
  • Every release has stakes. Every improvement is felt.
  • High expectations, low tolerance for politics, and a culture built on writing well and shipping with care.

OUR VALUES

We build the systems that power live event ticketing, and we hold a high bar for how we do it. Four principles run through everything:

  • Quality of life. Sustainable processes over heroics. Nobody should be a single point of failure, and nobody should be afraid to take a vacation.
  • Quality of code. Clarity over cleverness. If a teammate needs a long explanation to follow your code, it needs simplifying. Tests prove your work; they aren't optional.
  • Protection of production. Every change is reviewed, tested, and observable. We build with monitoring in mind from day one so we find problems before our users do.
  • Shared knowledge. We work across time zones, so we communicate in the open. Questions go in channels, not DMs, and one answer becomes shared knowledge.

ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES
We are an AI-native engineering team. Here is what that looks like in practice:

  • AI-assisted engineering. Every engineer uses Claude, Claude Code, Copilot, and agentic tooling as a routine part of their workflow.
  • Async-first. Most decisions happen in writing through Jira, Confluence, PR descriptions, design docs. We over-communicate on changes and under-communicate on noise.
  • Ownership mindset. Engineers are responsible for what they write and no code reaches production without review. Reviewers are co-owners.
  • Observability is part of "done." If the on-call engineer can't understand a system without reading source, more logging, metrics, and dashboards are needed.
  • Preservation of quality of code and life. We write code that is clean, tested, and maintainable so it serves us well over time, and we build sustainable processes so no one burns out or becomes a single point of failure.
  • Shared knowledge and continued education. We grow as a team by learning from each other through reviews, documentation, and collaboration.

OUR STACK & WAYS OF WORKING

  • VL1 (our core platform), B2B marketplace, distribution integrations, partner-facing APIs
  • Web & mobile clients, REST APIs, microservices
  • Languages: Ruby, Python, Typescript, C-Sharp
  • Frameworks and Technologies: Rails, Hanami, FastAPI, .NET, Postgres, DynamoDB, MSSQL Server, Docker, Terraform
  • Cloud Providers: AWS, Azure
  • Data: Snowflake, dbt, Dagster, AWS, Azure Data Factory, Sigma, Airflow
  • AI tooling: Anthropic / Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, in-house agentic workflows
  • Observability: Datadog, Grafana, Elastic/Kibana, OpsGenie
  • Collaboration: Jira, Confluence, GitHub, Slack, Miro
  • Async-first, agile cadences, distributed onshore + offshore teams

BENEFITS & PERKS

  • Comprehensive medical coverage
  • 100% employer-paid dental, vision, life, and disability insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid parental leave
  • Paid time off and company holidays
  • Employee wellness and professional development opportunities

Victory Live is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship status, marital status, disability, gender identity, gender expression, Veteran status, or another other characteristic protected by state, local or federal law.

Position Title: U.S. Director, Nuclear Energy

Reports to: Program Director, Nuclear Energy

Type: Full-time

Location: Remote, preference for someone living in the Washington, D.C. area

ABOUT CATF

Clean Air Task Force (CATF) is a nonprofit organisation working to safeguard against the worst impacts of climate change by catalysing the rapid global development and deployment of low-carbon energy and other climate-protecting technologies. This is accomplished through research and analysis, public advocacy leadership, and partnership with the private sector. CATF is highly respected for its deep expertise and research on energy and industrial systems and potential strategies, technologies, and policies that can radically shrink their impact on the planet’s atmosphere. Our team of experts and advocates (and global network of subject matter experts and civil society partners) put this research and knowledge into action by designing and enacting public policies that drive toward zero emissions. We also support policies and work directly with private industry to innovate in technology to make the path to zero emissions swift and affordable. CATF has offices in Boston, Washington D.C., and Brussels, with staff working virtually around the world.

ROLE

CATF is seeking an experienced and dynamic U.S. Director to join our Nuclear Energy Program. Reporting to the Program Director and managing a U.S. based senior policy manager, this individual will serve as an in-house subject matter expert in nuclear energy policy, with a focus on U.S federal and state advocacy, commercial nuclear energy industry, federal and state policy to support nuclear energy scaling, market dynamics, and regulatory ecosystems. The U.S. Director will support CATF’s nuclear energy strategy through policy advocacy, stakeholder engagement, project implementation, and outreach efforts, with an emphasis on advancing nuclear energy deployment in the U.S.

Key Functions and Responsibilities:

Nuclear policy and regulatory expertise

  • Serve as the in-house expert on nuclear policy, advocacy and related topics, particularly focused on the U.S. state and federal policy and regulatory ecosystems.
  • Identify, synthesize, and communicate key technical and economic trends across the U.S. nuclear energy sector, including industry players, government organizations, and regional markets.
  • Lead and manage policy research on nuclear energy technologies, delivering informed analysis regarding their contribution to U.S. climate and energy objectives.
  • Collaborate with CATF’s global nuclear fission energy team and multiple external stakeholders, engage in knowledge sharing and best practices.

Stakeholder engagement and outreach

  • Collaborate closely with the U.S. Advocacy team (federal, state, policy impact, and legal) on policy and advocacy activities related to nuclear energy, ensuring that CATF’s federal and state policy priorities are reflected in implementation strategies and campaigns.
  • Proactively engage external stakeholders, including federal and state policymakers, industry leaders, and NGOs, to drive policy and advocacy activities aligned with CATF’s nuclear energy strategy, projects, and initiatives in liaison with the U.S. Advocacy Team.
  • Lead outreach efforts to promote advanced nuclear technologies, coordinating efforts with U.S. government organizations, industry groups, non-governmental organizations and academic institutions in coordination with the Director for Nuclear Energy.
  • Serve as spokesperson on U.S. nuclear energy policy matters, representing CATF at high-level meetings, conferences, and public forums.
  • Engage with state-level policy and regulatory bodies to support regional nuclear energy deployment initiatives.

Project management and implementation

  • Develop and execute detailed work plans to ensure the successful implementation of U.S. nuclear energy strategy within CATF’s broader strategy
  • Lead hands-on execution of outreach, policy initiatives, and project implementation efforts that promote advanced nuclear technologies as part of the U.S. energy transition.
  • Oversee and produce relevant analyses and materials such as blogs, op-eds, factsheets and short white papers.
  • Oversee policy and analytical consultants as necessary.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with CATF teams to ensure U.S. nuclear energy initiatives are aligned with the organization’s goals and contribute to decarbonization efforts.

Commercial awareness

  • Maintain commercial awareness of U.S. nuclear energy market developments and ensure CATF’s activities are aligned with the evolving needs of the U.S. nuclear energy industry.

Leadership and collaboration

  • Provide strategic leadership in advancing nuclear energy initiatives in the U.S., reporting to and working closely with the U.S. Senior Manager and Director of Nuclear Energy.
  • Lead the U.S. nuclear energy program team, including managerial oversight of one employee.
  • Closely collaborate across the nuclear energy program team, in particular with the U.S. Senior Manager and Director of Nuclear Energy, as well as external partner organizations.
  • Cross-collaborate effectively in a matrix organization such as with communications, other programs, and cross-functional teams.
  • Engage in regular travel within the U.S. and periodic international travel to meet with stakeholders, attend industry events, and advocate for nuclear energy solutions.
  • Coach and collaborate with junior staff, providing guidance and fostering a collaborative work environment across CATF teams.
  • Ensure that U.S.-focused program activities are cost-effective and aligned with CATF’s budget.

Skills/Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of congressional and legislative processes and procedures.
  • Senior experience in the U.S. energy sector, with a strong focus on policy development and implementation, advocacy, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Extensive knowledge of energy industry, and policy and regulatory ecosystems, along with an established network in the sector.
  • Technical expertise is a plus but not required.
  • Ability to identify and communicate complex policy and regulatory trends across the U.S. nuclear energy sector.
  • Experience in driving federal and state policy and advocacy initiatives, engaging with government organizations and other stakeholders at the highest levels.
  • Experience leading a team, including management of resources, prioritizing employee growth development, and leading a team to deliver effective results.
  • Experience working across teams to ensure coordinated efforts on policy implementation.
  • Can do, positive and hands-on attitude in line with CATF core values of persistence, collaboration, and curiosity.

•International experience a plus.

  • Advanced degree (e.g., Master's, J.D. or Ph.D.) in energy policy, political science, government affairs, communications, or a related field.

•Passion for CATF’s mission.

Compensation and Location:

This is a full-time, remote position located in the Washington D.C. area with the expectation of being available to meet external stakeholders in D.C. as needed (approx. 1-2 times per week). CATF offers an excellent benefits package and an annual salary range of $144,863 - $185,000, depending on experience.

CATF provides equal employment opportunities.

Salary: $144,863 – $185,000 / year

jobs.description:
About Veedma

Veedma is a telehealth practice for men's hormonal and sexual health. We treat low testosterone, erectile dysfunction, and the symptoms men actually feel: libido, erection, energy, strength, and mood, in men 18 and up, fully online. Most low testosterone is secondary and reversible, so we find the cause first and stimulate the body's own production before resorting to TRT. Enclomiphene is the foundation; Tadalafil is co-prescribed when erectile or prostate symptoms coexist with low Free Testosterone. Testosterone replacement therapy is not a service we currently offer.

Small team, founder-led, AI-native by default. Both founders code in Claude Code every day, and internal tools get rewritten faster than they get maintained.

About the founders

You will work with both of us directly, every day.

Vladimir Kotlov, MD - Founder & CEO. Urologist by training (MD, 2014) with clinical experience in men's reproductive health. The clinical voice in every product call. ()

Victor Kuznetsov - Founder & CTO. 20+ years in software engineering and AI/ML. Previously Co-Founder & CTO of Yva.ai (people analytics, acquired by Visier). Owns the Veedma platform end-to-end today. ()

If the people you would be reporting to matters to you (it should), open both profiles before you apply.

What this role is not

Not SEO. Not paid acquisition. Not "manage the agency". Not "optimize the existing funnel by 3%". We don't have a media budget and we don't plan to start one. If you measure your seniority by the size of the paid budget you have managed, wrong seat.

What this role is

A builder who happens to do growth. Some bets are quick - a referral tweak, a landing page test, a podcast pitch that lands a guest spot, a creator DM that starts a real conversation. Others compound - a content engine, a community presence, a referral mechanism that gets sharper every month. You run several at once on different time horizons, and you build the tooling that makes that possible. Claude Code is your default surface; scrapers, agents, and scrappy internal tools are how the work gets done. Every channel is a system to reverse-engineer. Leverage comes from content the audience wants to share, creators who would talk about us without being paid to, communities we are part of, referral loops, and the patient experience itself.

You probably fit if

When you see a broken funnel, a slow page, a creator who would convert - your hand is already moving toward the keyboard. You don't wait for permission, a brief, a meeting, a vendor. You ship something rough today and learn from it tomorrow. You're personally interested in men's health, hormone optimization, sexual health, or longevity - the best growth people we've seen in this space were users of the category before they marketed it. You don't need to be a Veedma patient, but you should be the kind of person who would consider becoming one.

What you will own

  • How many tests are live this week. That, and patients added this quarter. Not dashboards.

  • New channels. Find ones nobody at Veedma is running - communities we should be in, podcasts where we should be guests, creators whose audience overlaps with ours, referral loops, adjacent practices. Prove or kill in 2-4 weeks.

  • Creator and community relationships. Find the voices in men's health, performance, and longevity who matter. Build relationships with them as a peer, not a buyer - we don't pay for posts. Turn it into a system, not a one-off ask.

  • Referrals and loops. Build the way existing patients bring new ones in. Instrument it. Make it sharper every month.

  • Landing pages and funnel tests. Write the copy, wire up the test, read the data.

  • Agents do the boring parts. By month 12, your routine work runs as agents you wrote. The day clears for figuring out what to build next.

What we are looking for

  • 10+ years in growth, organic acquisition, partnerships, or "founding growth" roles. Senior, hands-on. You have taken at least one brand from early traction to scale without leaning on paid media.

  • Healthcare is in your background. Most of those years were spent on a healthcare, telehealth, pharmacy, or supplements brand. Not "wellness-adjacent" SaaS. Not a fitness app. Real healthcare.

  • You want to stay in healthcare. You are not looking at us as a stop between two consumer-tech roles. When you describe your next 5 years, the words "health", "medicine", or "patients" show up unprompted.

  • Claude Code is your primary tool. Not "I have tried it", not "I use ChatGPT sometimes". 6+ months of daily use, 4+ hours per day. You write skills, wire up MCP integrations, compose sub-agents, automate the boring parts yourself. If you cannot describe your Claude Code workflow in concrete detail, wrong seat.

  • You build, you don't wait. Scrapers, prompt pipelines, no-code automations, ugly internal dashboards, scrappy landing pages - you ship them yourself. If engineering is the bottleneck, you have already routed around it.

  • When the data isn't there, you write the query. Cohort tables, funnel reports, ad-hoc digs in the warehouse - you do not file a ticket. Basic SQL.

  • Rules for marketing prescription telehealth in the US (FTC truth-in-advertising, no medical claims, HIPAA-adjacent) - known cold. You have shipped compliant content and creator briefs.

  • Copy is yours. No agency between you and the channel.

Nice to have

  • Worked at Hims, Ro, Hone, Maximus, or a similar DTC telehealth.

  • Hormone health, men's health, or sexual health specifically.

  • A repo, a Loom, or a writeup of an automation or growth hack you built and shipped.

How we operate

  • AI-native, not AI-curious. Both founders code in Claude Code every day. New hires do the same on day one. The bar for "should this be a tool" is hours, not weeks.

  • No queues, no tickets pointed at yourself. If you see it broken, you fix it. If a creator outreach script would save you four hours a week, you build it Friday. We don't wait.

  • Never idle. Always something being tested, a signal we're chasing, a part of the product getting tighter. A week without a new experiment is a broken week.

  • Signals over opinions. What patients message us, what support tickets say, where the funnel breaks, what creators reply, what the data shows - that sets the agenda. The product changes when the data says so, fast.

  • Straight line to the founders. No layers. You're in the room (Slack, Linear, the weekly call) where product, clinical, and business decisions happen. You're expected to weigh in.

  • Business-engaged or wrong seat. Not someone who clocks in, ships a brief, and goes home. Someone who reads the retention numbers, has a view on the pricing page, and pings us at 9pm when the data is off.

  • Async-first, US hours overlap. We ship every day at minimum.

    Compensation: $150,000-$190,000 per year plus 1.0%-1.25% equity. This role is remote in the United States and does not offer visa sponsorship.

Group Chief Financial Officer (Group CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and strategically minded Group Chief Financial Officer (Group CFO) to lead the financial strategy, performance, capital management, investment finance, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investments Group.

The Group CFO will have enterprise-wide responsibility for the Group's financial affairs, overseeing finance across subsidiaries, business units, investment entities, and operating companies.

As a key member of the Group Executive Leadership Team, the Group CFO will serve as a strategic advisor to the Group CEO, President, Board, Investment Committee, and other senior stakeholders, ensuring disciplined capital allocation, strong financial performance, balance-sheet resilience, regulatory compliance, and long-term shareholder value creation.

The role requires a sophisticated financial leader with experience across insurance, investment management, asset management, financial services, corporate finance, capital markets, and regulated financial institutions.

Key Responsibilities

1. Group Financial Strategy & Leadership

Develop and execute the Group's overall financial strategy in alignment with corporate objectives.

Provide strategic financial advice to the Group CEO, President, Board, and Executive Committee.

Establish Group-wide financial policies, standards, controls, and performance frameworks.

Ensure effective financial governance across subsidiaries, business units, joint ventures, and investment entities.

Lead the development of the Group's long-term financial and capital strategy.

2. Group P&L & Financial Performance

Assume overall responsibility for the Group's financial performance, profitability, balance sheet, cash flow, and capital position.

Monitor performance across all subsidiaries and business lines.

Drive sustainable earnings growth, expense efficiency, and return on capital.

Establish Group-wide financial KPIs and performance dashboards.

Challenge business-unit leadership on financial performance and corrective actions.

3. Financial Planning & Performance Management

Lead Group-wide annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning.

Develop financial scenarios and stress tests to support strategic decision-making.

Consolidate financial plans across subsidiaries and investment businesses.

Monitor actual performance against budgets, forecasts, and strategic objectives.

Strengthen management reporting and financial analytics.

4. Insurance Finance

Provide executive oversight of financial management across insurance businesses.

Monitor premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, underwriting results, and insurance profitability.

Oversee financial analysis of loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting margins.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk functions to understand financial exposures.

Provide financial input into product profitability, pricing, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions.

5. Investment & Asset Management Finance

Provide Group-level financial oversight of investment portfolios and investment businesses.

Partner with the Chief Investment Officer (CIO) and Investment Committee on investment strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, portfolio returns, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted performance.

Evaluate strategic investment opportunities and major portfolio decisions.

Ensure investment activities support the Group's liabilities, capital objectives, liquidity needs, and risk appetite.

6. Group Capital & Solvency Management

Lead Group-wide capital planning and capital optimization.

Monitor capital adequacy, solvency, leverage, liquidity, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize capital deployment across subsidiaries and business lines.

Assess the capital implications of acquisitions, investments, dividends, growth initiatives, and strategic transactions.

Partner with Risk and Actuarial leadership on capital and solvency assessments.

7. Asset-Liability Management

Provide executive oversight of asset-liability management (ALM) across relevant insurance and investment businesses.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support balance-sheet optimization and financial stress-testing initiatives.

8. Treasury & Liquidity

Lead Group treasury, liquidity, cash management, and banking relationships.

Establish Group-wide liquidity policies and funding strategies.

Optimize cash across subsidiaries while maintaining appropriate regulatory and operational liquidity.

Oversee debt facilities, guarantees, intercompany funding, and treasury risk.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

9. Capital Raising & Financing

Lead Group-level financing and capital-raising initiatives.

Develop relationships with banks, institutional investors, private equity firms, development-finance institutions, debt providers, and capital-market participants.

Oversee debt issuance, refinancing, capital injections, and other funding strategies.

Optimize the Group's capital structure and cost of capital.

Ensure funding capacity supports strategic growth.

10. M&A, Investments & Corporate Development

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, disposals, strategic investments, and joint ventures.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and deal structuring.

Assess the impact of transactions on earnings, capital, solvency, liquidity, and shareholder value.

Partner with the CEO and Board on major strategic transactions.

Oversee financial integration and post-transaction performance.

11. Group Financial Reporting & Consolidation

Ensure accurate and timely consolidated financial reporting across the Group.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and Board reporting.

Establish consistent accounting and reporting standards across subsidiaries.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Maintain strong relationships with external auditors and professional advisers.

12. Regulatory & Governance

Maintain strong financial governance across the Group.

Ensure compliance with applicable insurance, investment, corporate, tax, and financial regulations.

Manage relationships with regulators, auditors, rating agencies, and other external stakeholders.

Establish effective internal controls and financial policies.

Ensure appropriate governance across subsidiaries, SPVs, joint ventures, and investment entities.

13. Financial Risk Management

Establish and oversee the Group's financial risk-management framework.

Monitor market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, investment, interest-rate, FX, and operational financial risks.

Establish appropriate stress-testing and contingency-planning processes.

Work closely with the Group CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and business leaders to manage enterprise-wide risk.

14. Tax Strategy

Oversee Group-wide tax planning, compliance, reporting, and risk management.

Ensure appropriate tax governance across subsidiaries and jurisdictions.

Identify opportunities for legitimate tax efficiency.

Monitor changes in tax and regulatory requirements affecting the Group.

15. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, lenders, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Lead financial communications to the Board and key investors.

Support investor presentations, annual reports, strategic reviews, and capital-market activities.

Clearly communicate the Group's financial strategy, performance, and outlook.

16. Finance Transformation

Modernize the Group's finance operating model, systems, processes, and reporting infrastructure.

Strengthen ERP, FP&A, consolidation, business intelligence, and financial analytics capabilities.

Drive automation and digital transformation across finance.

Improve transparency and real-time visibility across subsidiaries and business units.

17. Leadership & Organizational Development

Lead the Group Finance function and senior finance leadership across subsidiaries.

Develop a high-performing, commercially focused finance organization.

Establish common standards, talent-development programs, and succession plans.

Build strong relationships with subsidiary CFOs and Finance Directors.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and value creation.

Key Performance Indicators

The Group CFO will be accountable for:

Group revenue and earnings growth

Group EBITDA / net income performance

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Insurance underwriting profitability

Combined ratio / loss ratio performance

Expense efficiency

Liquidity and cash-flow strength

Balance-sheet optimization

Cost of capital

Capital-raising effectiveness

M&A and strategic-investment performance

Budget and forecast accuracy

Regulatory and reporting compliance

Financial risk management

Shareholder value creation

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

18+ years of progressive finance experience, including substantial Group or enterprise-level leadership.

Previous experience as Group CFO, CFO, Deputy Group CFO, Group Finance Director, Finance Director, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, investment management, asset management, banking, pensions, reinsurance, or diversified financial services.

Proven experience managing complex group structures, subsidiaries, investment entities, and regulated businesses.

Strong understanding of insurance financial reporting, capital and solvency requirements, investment portfolios, and balance-sheet management.

Demonstrated experience in capital allocation, treasury, liquidity, financial planning, and enterprise risk.

Experience working directly with Boards, CEOs, regulators, auditors, investors, lenders, and rating agencies.

Preferred Experience

Previous Group CFO experience within a diversified insurance or investment group.

Experience covering both insurance operations and investment/asset-management businesses.

Exposure to life insurance, general insurance, reinsurance, pensions, or institutional investment.

Experience managing significant investment portfolios and ALM.

Proven experience with M&A, capital raising, restructuring, strategic investments, or international expansion.

Experience across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory environments.

Experience working with international institutional investors or rating agencies.

Education & Professional Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related discipline.

Professional qualification such as CA, ACCA, CPA, CMA, CFA, or equivalent strongly preferred.

MBA or Master's degree in Finance/Business is advantageous.

Additional insurance, investment, actuarial, or risk-management qualifications are desirable.

Core Competencies

Group Financial Leadership

Corporate Finance

Insurance Finance

Investment Finance

Capital & Solvency Management

Asset-Liability Management

Treasury & Liquidity

Financial Planning & Analysis

Investment Analysis

Financial Modeling

Capital Allocation

M&A & Corporate Development

Regulatory Reporting

Risk Management

Investor Relations

Corporate Governance

Finance Transformation

Leadership Characteristics

The successful Group CFO will be:

Strategic, commercially astute, and financially rigorous

Comfortable operating across complex group structures

Strong in capital allocation and investment decisions

Experienced in highly regulated environments

A sophisticated communicator at Board and investor level

Strong in balance-sheet and liquidity management

Comfortable challenging business leaders and driving accountability

Able to balance growth, profitability, capital, liquidity, and risk

An effective partner to the CEO, CIO, CRO, Chief Actuary, and subsidiary CEOs

A transformational leader capable of building a world-class Group Finance function
